name: Password managers
intro: Where moving to a new phone and autofill are reliable, and where the authenticator fails when you need it most.

apps.title: aWallet Cloud Password Manager
apps.verdict: A reliable offline password manager with cross-platform sync via cloud storage. The main weakness is no iCloud support, and occasional sync failures can lead to data loss.
apps.loved: Simplicity and stability over many years, simultaneous support for Android and iOS, encryption via Google Drive and Dropbox, easy transfer when switching phones.
apps.weak: No iCloud sync, periodic Google Drive errors (404), after iOS updates it sometimes locks access with no way to reset the master password, some users dislike the interface refresh.
apps.whoFor: Users who want a simple, affordable password manager without a subscription and with sync between Android and iPhone.

apps.title: Strongbox - Password Manager
apps.verdict: A KeePass-compatible password manager with an open database format, Wi-Fi sync, and security key support. Quality declined after a change of ownership: previously hidden bugs have become more frequent, and upgrade prompts now chase even Pro users.
apps.loved: Open KeePass format (no lock-in), solid iCloud sync, Yubikey and passkeys support, autofill, export to standard formats, lifetime license.
apps.weak: Quality has slipped since the app changed hands: crashes on database open, upgrade pop-ups for Pro users, passkeys issues (crashes on save), cross-platform purchases don't sync across devices.
apps.whoFor: Technically savvy Apple users who want an open database format and prefer not to rely on a cloud service.

quotes.text: I've been using this app for a few years now, and even bought the lifetime license. It's been great, except for passkeys. For some reason this app breaks whenever I try to save passkeys from every one of my iOS apps to my db (it both fails to save the key and crashes upon retry).

apps.title: KeePassium (KeePass passwords)
apps.verdict: The best choice for storing passwords offline in KeePass format. Its strength is full privacy with no cloud server required, its weakness is unreliable autofill and iCloud sync issues.
apps.loved: Fully offline with no data shared with third parties. Passkeys and TOTP support. Independent security audit by Cure53. Actively maintained. Fast import.
apps.weak: Autofill is unreliable and sometimes fails in banking apps. Issues with iCloud Drive after iOS updates. Occasional hangs when loading the database. No native Android or Windows clients.
apps.whoFor: Technical users who already use KeePass and want to keep their data on-device only.

apps.title: Dashlane Password Manager
apps.verdict: A mature cross-platform password manager with a real long-term user base. Strong point is reliable sync and a solid password generator. The main complaint is an aggressive paywall and problems when the free plan was dropped.
apps.loved: Sync across all devices, strong password generator, family plan with shared access, autofill works consistently.
apps.weak: Holds passwords hostage on non-payment, unclear login flow for existing accounts, transferring to a new device can be tricky, passwords disappear after reconnection, browser extension may be blocked by corporate policies.
apps.whoFor: Users willing to pay for a cross-platform manager with a convenient family plan.

quotes.text: Dashlane not only remembers my passwords, but logs me in automatically. With my new iPhone X, I have had a few glitches where my password is no longer valid. This was fairly simple to fix by updating my password, which probably needed to be done anyway. It not only stores my passwords, but promp
Been using DashLane for 6 years now with 5 family members all using it as well. It seamlessly updates my passwords no matter what platform I'm using and allows me to login into all my accounts.

Used this app for years, but changed phones and it was absolutely impossible to transfer my info over. Cancelled membership. Thank goodness I have Apple's password keeper, too. Pass on this one folks.

Been using DashLane for 6 years now with 5 family members all using it as well. It seamlessly updates my passwords no matter what platform I'm using. My parents are getting older and sharing passwords and having them on the same platform as me makes thing
I like the app, but since dashlane switched to browser extensions(which my employer banned) it has become useless for work purposes. Will look for something else.

All my passwords are in the cloud. If my ISP fails, I have no access to my passwords. It used to be I could download a comma delineated text file of all my logins just for this very reason, but I cannot find a way to do that now.

Love this app! I love that it syncs all my devices and love that I don't have to try and remember my passwords. The best part is the password generator. It treks me when passwords are weak and creates a new one when I want it to.

apps.title: eWallet - Password Manager
apps.verdict: A market veteran with a twenty-year track record: stable, simple, no subscription. The main pain point is that sync between devices is unreliable, especially without a desktop in the mix.
apps.loved: Decades of reliable operation, support helps with data migration, works across platforms (Mac, PC, iPhone), no subscription, straightforward interface.
apps.weak: Sync without a PC doesn't work or is unreliable, no automatic cloud backup, can't enlarge password text, no image storage within entries, OneDrive integration is broken.
apps.whoFor: Apple ecosystem users with a PC who want reliable storage without a subscription and don't need modern features like passkeys.

quotes.text: So riddle me this Batman I'm trying to sync my iPhone with my iPad without going through my desktop computer which I don't use anymore. How come I can't do it?
Rely on for secure storage of passwords and other private info with cloud update across all devices. Seriously deficient in that there is no image storage within an entry.

apps.title: SafeInCloud 1
apps.verdict: A time-tested manager with good sync via your own cloud account, but it suffers from passwords disappearing after updates and aggressive new paid tiers appearing after each update.
apps.loved: Works across multiple browsers and devices, free basic tier, stores data in a user-chosen cloud (not the company's servers), regular updates.
apps.weak: Passwords disappear after updates without warning, sync between devices is unreliable, the company repeatedly introduces new paid tiers on top of already-purchased licenses, problems on Windows 11, family sharing is hard to set up.
apps.whoFor: Users with a single device or a small number of passwords who want to store data in their own cloud without a subscription.

quotes.text: I love this app and have been using it for years! The only grip I have is my wife and I have found it difficult to share the same database in cloud storage. At various times the databases have gotten out of sync and we have not been able to get them merged back again.

apps.title: Bitwarden Password Manager
apps.verdict: The best free open-source password manager for the price-to-features ratio, but recent updates introduced serious bugs: the master password sometimes refuses to work, TOTP behind a paywall feels greedy, and cross-device sync is slow.
apps.loved: Completely free with no ads, open-source, works on all platforms, no upsell pressure.
apps.weak: Master password periodically fails for no apparent reason, TOTP is paid-only, slow sync, a bug shows phantom TOTP codes on entries that don't have one.
apps.whoFor: Technically minded users who want a solid free manager and can tolerate occasional bugs.

quotes.text: I like using Bitwarden, but sometimes it's buggy on picking out the password for websites and it's very slow to sync between different devices

Master password sometimes flat out fails. App will not accept it but same pass on desktop works, or desktop doesn't but website does. Website frequently also goes into a login loop on mobile and is correct but will not proceed to the actual vault.
It doesn't make sense you would charge to use a feature so common such as 2FA.
Normally pretty good password manager. Lately it's had some weird bugs. For example, it is showing TOTP codes for entries that don't have one, even the recent fix didn't change this.

apps.title: pwSafe 2 - Password Safe
apps.verdict: A mature PasswordSafe-format manager with cross-platform support and a responsive developer, but switching to a new iPhone repeatedly breaks database access unacceptable for a password storage tool.
apps.loved: PasswordSafe format ensures compatibility with Windows and Mac, developer responds to bug reports and ships updates, Dropbox and iCloud sync, users have run the app for more than 10 years.
apps.weak: Switching to a new iPhone has caused database loss for multiple users, cloud backup is pushed with aggressive notifications, local iOS-to-desktop sync is inconvenient, the UI is dated, some versions confused users with duplicate database copies.
apps.whoFor: Experienced users who need PasswordSafe-compatible format and cross-platform access, and who are prepared to keep a separate backup of their database.

apps.title: Cryptical
apps.verdict: A password generation utility from a Germany-based developer with EU-compliant privacy practices. Works well as a companion to a primary password manager, but has a bug: it generates passwords longer than the requested character count.
apps.loved: Works reliably for years, EU-standard privacy policy, developer responds to support requests, no data collection, the core password-generation function does its job.
apps.weak: Generates passwords longer than the specified length, doesn't honor all selected criteria for short passwords, no cloud backup, annoying review-request pop-ups, Face ID enters an infinite loop after updates.
apps.whoFor: Users who need a simple password generator without data sharing, as a companion to a primary vault.

quotes.text: App is good but dont know what happen after the latest upgrade no able to access stays in a loop in the login using face id, no the issue remain 1/29/2026

apps.title: Password Manager: Safe
apps.verdict: SafeInCloud under a new name: a proven manager with cross-platform cloud sync, but recent updates broke familiar interface elements and frustrated long-time users.
apps.loved: In use for over 10 years by many users, passkeys support, sync via Google Drive and iCloud, works on Android and iOS, solid support.
apps.weak: Removed the alphabetical scroll index, an aggressive Premium purchase banner on every launch, passkeys don't work on Mac or in browser extensions, licensing issues when switching platforms, crashes after the latest update.
apps.whoFor: Android and iPhone users who want a reliable cross-platform manager without a third-party cloud subscription.

quotes.text: Works well but without passkey support on MacOS and Windows browser extension. It leaves me to shy away from recommending to others.

apps.title: Sticky Password Manager & Safe
apps.verdict: One of the few password managers that offer local Wi-Fi sync with no cloud involved. Good for privacy-conscious users, but autofill is buggy, there's no password generator, and no 2FA support.
apps.loved: Offline sync over local network with no cloud data transfer, lifetime license at a fair price, cross-platform (Windows, iOS, Android), stable for long-term users.
apps.weak: No built-in password generator at the point of entry creation, no 2FA support, autofill sometimes fills in the old password when you change it, Mac import is problematic, installs Rosetta without warning.
apps.whoFor: Users who fundamentally don't want passwords in the cloud and are willing to sync over their home network.

quotes.text: Have used across platforms for almost 2 decades. App is well supported- simple - clean - stable. Credit to developers

apps.title: Keeper Password Manager
apps.verdict: A full-featured password manager with a long history and a real base of loyal users, but with annual price hikes and a migration path designed to be painful.
apps.loved: Secure storage with notes and attachments, cross-platform sync, long-term users praise stability and support.
apps.weak: Price has climbed to $42 $91 per year and keeps rising, migration is intentionally difficult, an 'optimization' step on every launch freezes the app for minutes, can't cancel a subscription from within the app.
apps.whoFor: Users willing to pay a premium price who don't plan on switching.

quotes.text: The only reason I keep using this trash is momentum, migration out of this ecosystem is unavailable.

I store everything in my Keeper. With five kids and a mother who can't remember any passwords, I have every piece of data in my hand at all times. BUT, they limit me for the number of downloads such as dog vaccination papers

apps.title: Proton Pass - Password Manager
apps.verdict: A serious password manager from the Proton team with a strong privacy reputation, but the iOS client is unstable: autofill works intermittently and Face ID can get stuck in a loop.
apps.loved: Meaningful free tier, built-in email aliases, cross-platform support, Proton's trusted privacy reputation, convenient family sharing.
apps.weak: Autofill crashes or fails in Safari and Firefox Mobile, Face ID loops after updates, no passkeys on macOS, can't import Safari passwords on iOS without a desktop browser, every new entry triggers a review prompt.
apps.whoFor: Users already in the Proton ecosystem who care about privacy and email aliases and can tolerate rough edges in the iOS client.

quotes.text: Recently the app has been crashing while attempting to auto fill a password in safari and Fire fox mobile which not only feels very clunky but sometimes it's so inconsistent it makes that function unusable.
It's such a massive feature gap to not have support for Passkeys on macOS.

This app provides no way to import passwords from an iOS device. If you are using only an iPhone, there is no way to import the files the you can export from safari. The instructions tell you to download another browser that supports the proton extensions, but apple doesn't allow extensions on any t

apps.title: oneSafe+ password manager
apps.verdict: A mature offline password manager with a loyal user base that has stuck around for years. The main pain point: migrating from version 5 to version 6 broke backups, and support has effectively gone silent.
apps.loved: Rich entry fields, tags and folders, Wi-Fi import and export, many template formats, works without cloud storage.
apps.weak: Backups are incompatible between versions 5 and 6, no export to standard formats (proprietary only), no developer support, freezes on iOS 18, no backup reminder.
apps.whoFor: Users who want an offline vault without cloud dependencies and with a flexible entry structure, and who accept the risk of data loss during updates.

quotes.text: You cannot export PWs other than to proprietary so x format, so once you use OneSafe, you are stuck with it. In my case I want to move to Apple Passwords, and it looks like I have to do it manually for 370 passwords

apps.title: Duo Mobile
apps.verdict: A corporate 2FA tool that just works until it doesn't. The biggest failure: transferring accounts to a new phone is nearly impossible, and push notifications are unreliable.
apps.loved: Years of stable operation with minimal fuss, quick login confirmation, a sense of security for corporate access.
apps.weak: No real account transfer between devices, push notifications drop out and force manual code entry, frequent forced updates, no backup login method besides a phone number.
apps.whoFor: Corporate users whose company requires Duo and who have no choice.

quotes.text: We use this app for our office. Most of the time it works great... if you have an internet connection. There is an "offline" option but it's garbage! When my employees travel, they're unable to unlock their pcs b/c Duo doesn't have an internet connection.

apps.title: Codebook Password Manager
apps.verdict: A veteran dating back to Palm Pilot days: strong AES-256 encryption, flexible storage, but version 5 broke sync for a significant number of users and the new sync key mechanism is confusing.
apps.loved: AES-256-CBC with HMAC-SHA512, 256,000 PBKDF2 rounds, no proprietary servers (data stays with the user), flexible entry structure including photos and documents, decades of reliable use.
apps.weak: Sync broke after updating to version 5 for many users, the sync key mechanism is confusing and poorly documented, autofill performs poorly, no Face ID in the base version, no recovery if the master password is lost.
apps.whoFor: Technically savvy users who value local storage with military-grade encryption and aren't afraid to configure sync manually.

quotes.text: Great app and very easy to use. One very important thing to remember though. WRITE DOWN YOUR MASTER PASSWORD!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! If for some reason you forget or lose your master password. Don't bother trying to get any help. Just uninstall the app, re-install it and start over. There is now way to recov

apps.title: Norton Password Manager
apps.verdict: A free password manager within the Norton ecosystem, stable enough for basic tasks, but no passkeys support, occasional connection drops, and constant upsell offers.
apps.loved: Free for basic use, easy to get started, reliably stores passwords for most sites.
apps.weak: No passkeys support, unstable connection on mobile, intrusive survey pop-ups, autofill doesn't work on some sites.
apps.whoFor: Existing Norton subscribers who need a simple manager without extra cost.

quotes.text: Where is the support for passkeys? Been a long time user, but may have to switch for this reason alone.

apps.title: RoboForm Password Manager
apps.verdict: One of the oldest password managers on the market, strong on core features (storage, SafeNotes), but the UX is dated, autofill is unpredictable, and update 9.9.1 broke launch for some users.
apps.loved: Years of reliability for loyal users, note and form storage, cross-platform access.
apps.weak: Autofill doesn't always trigger and doesn't offer to save an updated password, search settings don't persist, weak customer support, some users lost all their data.
apps.whoFor: Users with large archives of notes and forms who can accept an outdated UX.

quotes.text: Does not automatically send me to selected website. I frequently have to look up the password myself. Also inconsistent with saving updated passwords. Sometimes asks if I want to save it and sometimes does not.

I've only have to remember one password and I can have a unique, extremely hard, password for every login. Roboform makes security and form filling easy. I also make extensive use of the safenotes feature to record sensitive information behind a secure password. Great pr

apps.title: aWallet Password Manager
apps.verdict: A cross-platform password manager with category support and Face ID that worked reliably for years. The problem: multiple waves of monetization changes stripped paid users of features they'd already paid for, without explanation.
apps.loved: Categories for organizing entries, Face ID (when it works), simple interface, good fit for older users, long-standing loyal user base.
apps.weak: Touch ID unexpectedly moved behind a paywall for users who had already paid, Android purchases don't carry over to iOS, CSV import only works through an iTunes directory, no master password reset.
apps.whoFor: iOS users who want a simple categorized vault and can accept inconsistent monetization.

quotes.text: Latest update prevents me from using Touch ID to login. If you want to use Touch ID, it gives a prompt to require you to pay for subscription. I paid for the app and it used to have Touch ID. Now they removed this convenience just to push you into buying subscription. Greedy developer!

apps.title: Password Manager-
apps.verdict: An old local password manager with no cloud and a devoted following, but search crashes the app, backup is broken, and the developer doesn't respond to support requests.
apps.loved: Works locally without cloud, simple and fast, long-term users are satisfied with everyday stability, convenient entry organization.
apps.weak: Search crashes the app, Wi-Fi backup and restore don't work, no export to standard formats (CSV, XLS), developer ignores inquiries, support email is no longer functional, hard to sync between devices.
apps.whoFor: Users who need an offline password manager without a subscription and don't expect technical support.

apps.title: Google Authenticator
apps.verdict: A minimalist 2FA authenticator that works fine until you change your phone. Losing all codes when switching devices without manual transfer is a systemic problem known to every long-time user.
apps.loved: No ads or bloat, Google account sync now helps when transferring, simple interface.
apps.weak: Before cloud sync was added, migration was a disaster, codes occasionally vanish, no way to organize entries into folders or rename them, the QR camera doesn't work for some users.
apps.whoFor: Google ecosystem users who want basic TOTP with no extras.

quotes.text: This is generally good, but if you forget to migrate things manually before getting a new phone, your accounts are forever lost

I only click into the app to get a code when needed. Logged in one day and every single one of my accounts was no longer there. No codes for anything, and guess what? Now I can't access anything else. DO NOT USE THIS APP

apps.title: Passwords
apps.verdict: Apple's built-in password manager that works invisibly for most users, but regularly loses passwords after iOS updates and handles import and export poorly.
apps.loved: Zero setup on Apple devices, iCloud sync, notifications for compromised passwords, family plan sharing.
apps.weak: Passwords disappear after OS updates, no proper export, weak support for non-Apple platforms, QR login is unreliable, autofill doesn't work everywhere.
apps.whoFor: Users who live entirely in the Apple ecosystem and don't need cross-platform support.

quotes.text: Sharing made things much much better
I was notified that 3 of my passwords were comprised in a data leak!
Apple generated a random password for me, but this app said that "RXF345-BMA-810" would be easy to guess?!??!

apps.title: Password Manager - mSecure
apps.verdict: A mature password manager with a long track record that has badly degraded in recent versions: forced upgrade ads for paying users, Face ID moved behind a paywall, Dropbox sync crashes the app.
apps.loved: Reliably stores data over years, simple interface for basic tasks, ability to attach photos to entries.
apps.weak: Face ID is paid-only, aggressive upgrade banners even for subscribers, crashes during Dropbox sync, losing the QR recovery code locks users out of their vault entirely.
apps.whoFor: Long-time users who don't need biometrics and can tolerate aggressive marketing.

quotes.text: Very happy to pay the extremely reasonable price for a Premium subscription. I attach photos to entries, and it saves so much time. mSecure has been my trustworthy password & sensitive data keeper for many, many years. Never had even a hiccup of a problem.

apps.title: NordPass: Password Manager
apps.verdict: A recognizable password manager from Nord that works as a vault, but with irritating systemic issues: it constantly asks for the master password, autofill is inconsistent across sites, the Safari extension was removed without notice, and importing passwords from iPhone is not supported.
apps.loved: Strong encryption, cross-platform support, a wide range of supported data types, relatively clear interface.
apps.weak: Constant re-authentication kills convenience, autofill skips saving changes, Safari extension dropped without warning, can't import iPhone passwords directly.
apps.whoFor: Users already in the Nord ecosystem who don't need seamless autofill and can live with frequent master password prompts.

quotes.text: You can't autosave. So if you add/change a password, you need to make sure you manually save it. Makes this product useless in my book.
Can't import my passwords from my iPhone into Nord. Appears I have to manually enter all websites data and app data into Nord

apps.title: My Eyes Only Password Manager
apps.verdict: A functional password manager with sync and support that actually responds. The main problem: repeated subscription price hikes of 33 100% in a single year pushed many loyal users to leave.
apps.loved: Good support (the director personally responded to bugs), many categories, years of reliability for some users, Syncryption backups.
apps.weak: Recurring price increases of 33 100%, data loss during updates, freezes during alphabetical navigation, bugs after recent updates, the app switched to Spanish with no way to change the language.
apps.whoFor: Users who need sync and live support, and are willing to revisit their subscription regularly.

apps.title: Password Safe and Manager
apps.verdict: A simple standalone password manager with a clean design, but the lack of cross-device sync is a critical failure for a product of this type.
apps.loved: Intuitive interface, a sense of security from local storage, developer is personally reachable (Robert responds to questions), reasonable PRO pricing.
apps.weak: No real cross-device sync, switching from Android to iOS or changing phones results in data loss, no fingerprint authentication in the base version, license doesn't transfer between platforms, support is slow to respond.
apps.whoFor: Single-device users who want an isolated offline password vault with no cloud.

apps.title: Enpass Password Manager
apps.verdict: A solid concept with user-owned encrypted storage, but the product is degrading due to intrusive features and reputational damage from changing terms without notice.
apps.loved: User owns the vault and chooses where to store it (iCloud, Dropbox, etc.). Works on all platforms. Passkeys and TOTP support. Good value at the lifetime price.
apps.weak: Forced master password entry on a timer that can't be disabled even in settings. Sync regularly breaks (iPad and Mac). The app forgets a purchased subscription and shows ads. Users report data being transferred to Apple Passwords without consent.
apps.whoFor: Users who want to own their vault and not depend on a provider's cloud, and who can tolerate technical rough edges.

apps.title: Zoho Vault - Password Manager
apps.verdict: A corporate password manager from Zoho with a solid web version and Chrome extension, but the iOS app crashes regularly and loses sessions. Acceptable for team use via browser.
apps.loved: Free tier for personal use, good scalability for teams, convenient web version and Chrome extension, centralized password management.
apps.weak: App freezes and crashes on iOS 16 and iOS 13 Pro, constantly prompts for master password re-entry, Safari autofill doesn't work, support brushes off problems.
apps.whoFor: Small teams and enterprise users who work through a browser not for reliable daily use on iPhone.

apps.title: 1Password: Password Manager
apps.verdict: Once the gold standard of password managers, now with aggressive monetization: forced subscription instead of a one-time license, regular price increases, UX regressions (removed search, complicated navigation), and support that takes days to respond.
apps.loved: Good cross-platform coverage for long-time users, solid encryption, Travel Mode.
apps.weak: Price jumped from $30 to $75 for the family plan, quick search was removed from the home screen, support responds in days or weeks, accounts can be frozen without explanation and there's no phone support.
apps.whoFor: Corporate teams with an IT budget individual users will get the same from Bitwarden or Apple Passwords for free.

quotes.text: It's great until you have lost memory of your main password and then youre Screwed. Im going back to paper and pen.

As someone in their 40s, not only do I appreciate not having to remember my own passwords, but this app has saved me hours upon hours of tech support for my parents. My dad passed recently and unexpectedly, and being able to access his accounts has made the logistics of death so much easier than it

apps.title: Password Manager iPassSafe
apps.verdict: A simple offline password manager with a long-term audience, but a critical problem: data disappears when switching devices or after iOS updates, and support is practically unreachable.
apps.loved: Simple, intuitive interface, works without internet, Dropbox and Wi-Fi sync support, loyal users have relied on it for years.
apps.weak: Data is lost when switching devices or after iOS updates with no way to recover it, Face ID can permanently block access, no search across entries, support goes silent on inquiries.
apps.whoFor: Users who have maintained a long-running database and don't switch devices for new users the risk of total data loss is too high.

apps.title: LastPass Password Manager
apps.verdict: Once a respectable password manager, now disappointing its user base after restricting the free plan to a single device type and letting support quality slide. Loyal users are migrating to Bitwarden.
apps.loved: Organized storage, convenient to have all passwords in one place, autofill works for most sites.
apps.weak: No cross-platform access without a paid subscription, frequent random sign-outs, support is unreachable when MFA is locked, mobile interface is clunky, the app prompts to save a password that's already there.
apps.whoFor: Users who have already committed their data and are slow to migrate.

quotes.text: No one to call to reset my password and it's a paid account and waiting to change phones but about you lose your po password

apps.title: Password Manager Data Vault
apps.verdict: Once a reliable password manager, now without updates for years: a systemic bug where changes don't save on the first attempt and complete developer silence make it risky for storing important credentials.
apps.loved: Works on Mac and iPhone, no subscription, Apple Watch support for quick password lookup, Wi-Fi sync, worked reliably for old users for years.
apps.weak: Changes don't save on the first try and must be entered twice, the app hasn't been updated in 3 5 years, support doesn't respond to emails for months, no passkeys or modern security standards, sync is unreliable, data sometimes disappears.
apps.whoFor: No one who is adding new passwords now the product has effectively been abandoned by its developer.

quotes.text: This used to be a nice app and for the last year it has been super glitchy. I put in a new password but it doesn't save unless I enter 4 different times. Even sometimes when it saves it is gone later. I am DONE with this app!!!

apps.title: True Key™ by McAfee
apps.verdict: McAfee's password manager that has degraded: autofill stopped working, the app crashes, and sessions reset on their own. It used to be decent, but now it's outclassed by Apple's built-in options.
apps.loved: Multi-factor authentication, long-time users noted reliability, unlimited notes even on the free tier.
apps.weak: Autofill doesn't work, the app crashes on login, it signs itself out before the set timeout, you can't change your email or master password, the free tier is capped at 15 passwords, no dark web monitoring or 2FA, the desktop version has been shut down.
apps.whoFor: Existing McAfee subscribers who get the manager bundled in. New users should look elsewhere.

quotes.text: Overall It's a good app for any standard users. Reason I didn't give 5 star because it lacks following: no dark web monitoring, no 2FA ( but it has MFA), Desktop version of TrueKey is no longer supported, Password sharing is not an option.

apps.title: iRemember - Password Manager
apps.verdict: A simple offline password manager for non-technical users, hampered by chronic crashes, data loss, and unresponsive support.
apps.loved: Simple alphabetical organization. Works without cloud. Long-term users value reliability when it's working.
apps.weak: The app periodically crashes and won't open, sometimes losing all saved passwords. No backup. Support doesn't respond to emails. No biometrics in older versions. Alphabetical sorting broke after an update.
apps.whoFor: Users who need the simplest possible password list with no autofill or cloud but only if the app is stable.

apps.title: iPassworder Password Manager
apps.verdict: A bare-bones offline password vault with a 10-entry limit on the free tier. The main problem: no export and no recovery, so forgetting the master password means losing everything.
apps.loved: Simple interface, works after a one-time payment without a subscription, Face ID support.
apps.weak: The 10-password cap is hidden until after installation, no data export, no master password reset, one user reports password leaks, complaints about data loss on device changes.
apps.whoFor: Users with a very small number of passwords, willing to accept the risk of losing everything if they forget the master password.

apps.title: UniFi Verify
apps.verdict: A 2FA authenticator exclusively for the Ubiquiti ecosystem not a general-purpose tool. Crashes on iOS while scrolling, total loss of all 2FA accounts when switching phones with no recovery path, unreliable Apple Watch authentication, and zero documentation.
apps.loved: Works with push notifications to confirm logins on Ubiquiti devices, Apple Watch integration in theory.
apps.weak: Crashes while scrolling on current iOS versions, no account transfer when switching phones, Apple Watch doesn't confirm requests, no documentation, works only with Ubiquiti.
apps.whoFor: Ubiquiti equipment owners who don't hit the specific iOS compatibility issues. For everyone else, there's no reason to use it.

apps.title: Password Manager: Passible
apps.verdict: A password manager with a long history of loyal users that is now in a degraded state: a Face ID loop, broken export, and unresponsive support make it a risky place to store credentials.
apps.loved: Simple interface, credit card storage alongside passwords, worked reliably for some users for years.
apps.weak: Face ID loop blocks app entry (multiple reviews from 2024 2026), export and cross-device sync don't work, users lose all data after switching phones, the support email bounces, no password recovery.
apps.whoFor: Current users with a working version should back up their data immediately and move to another tool.

quotes.text: This app was great until recently. I had dozens of my passwords stored here for home and work. Recently the app was glitching on face recognition mode. Kept going cycling through face recognition over and over. Would not accept it and would not let me put a password in instead.

apps.title: My Passwords Manager
apps.verdict: A simple password vault that moved Face ID behind a paywall without warning, leaving long-time users without convenient login. That complaint accounts for about 60% of all reviews.
apps.loved: Simple interface, data persists after reinstallation for some users, straightforward navigation.
apps.weak: Face ID and Touch ID moved to a paid tier without notifying existing users, no support when contacted, Pro status lost after updates, no way to transfer data without paying extra when switching phones.
apps.whoFor: Users with minimal requirements who are willing to enter their master password manually every time.

quotes.text: I have had facial recognition with this app for years. Recently you deactivated this unless I pay extra for it. That sucks.

apps.title: Passwords Cloud
apps.verdict: A basic password vault with no advanced features: no real search, the lock password disables itself spontaneously, and the free tier is capped at 8 10 entries.
apps.loved: Long-term users report reliability for simple use. Transfers to a new phone.
apps.weak: App lock password disables itself after a restart. Can't delete entries in some versions. Free tier is capped at 8 passwords with no prior notice. No alphabetical search. Small font.
apps.whoFor: Users with minimal requirements who need to store literally a handful of passwords and don't care about locking security.

apps.title: Password Manager Finger Print Lock for iPhone Safe
apps.short: Password Manager Finger Print Lock for iPhone Safe
apps.verdict: An abandoned app with no active maintenance: after iOS updates it regularly stops opening entries and loses data. Some users stay out of long habit, but continuing to use it is risky.
apps.loved: Simple, user-friendly interface for storing passwords, worked steadily for long-term users before recent iOS updates.
apps.weak: After iOS updates the app stops working and won't open entries, data is lost with no recovery option, the developer appears to have stopped supporting the product, backups are incompatible between versions.
apps.whoFor: Not recommended for new installs the app is effectively abandoned and unreliable.

apps.title: SecureSafe Password Manager
apps.verdict: A Swiss password manager with a long history that has been broken on mobile since 2024: Face ID doesn't work, every login redirects to a browser, subscriptions expire without warning. Legacy praise holds the store rating up, but the current user experience is unacceptable.
apps.loved: Worked reliably for years, web version is accessible, document storage is available.
apps.weak: Face ID has been broken for over a year, every login goes through the browser, no expiration notice for subscriptions, support responds only with form letters.
apps.whoFor: Not recommended for anyone right now until the mobile app is fixed.

apps.title: Password Manager - Secure
apps.loved: Some users praise the easy initial setup and the presence of a secure photo vault.
apps.weak: App crashes immediately after entering the password, forced video ads appeared after updates, no way to reset a forgotten master password, support doesn't respond, paid VIP version stops working.
apps.whoFor: Not recommended for anyone unreliability and absent support make it dangerous for storing passwords.

apps.title: LastPass Authenticator
apps.verdict: An authenticator that's supposed to make login easier but in practice makes it harder: codes disappear, moving to a new phone requires simultaneous access to the old phone and a computer, and push authorization gets stuck in an endless loop.
apps.loved: Push notification on computer login is convenient, iCloud backup works for users who have it set up correctly.
apps.weak: Loss of all codes without warning, extremely difficult migration between devices, the app gets stuck in an approval loop, Stage Manager broken on iPad.
apps.whoFor: Only single-device users with a working LastPass ecosystem everyone else should use Authy or a built-in authenticator.

quotes.text: Moving from old phone to new phone isn't just a task, it is a full time job. Last pass has turned 2 factor authentication into 5 factor authentication when you include the need to log into my account on the PC in addition to the authenticator and the LP app on both phones.
Just all my codes that I just entered disappeared

apps.title: SplashID Safe Password Manager
apps.verdict: Once a popular password manager with a 20-year history, now in a state of decline: the app crashes, sync is broken, and support is silent.
apps.loved: Supports storing arbitrary data beyond passwords (PIN codes, combination locks). Some users value local sync without third-party cloud.
apps.weak: App crashes on current versions of macOS and iOS. Sync doesn't work. Data is lost when moving between versions. No normal way to cancel a subscription through the interface. A complaint was upheld by the Better Business Bureau. No new features for several years.
apps.whoFor: Not recommended for anyone switching to a modern alternative is the better move.

apps.title: Authenticator App - OneAuth
apps.verdict: Zoho's MFA app that is convenient in theory for the Zoho ecosystem but in practice suffers from unreliable push notifications, a freezing interface, and a mandatory notification permission without which some features don't work.
apps.loved: Good integration with Zoho accounts, supports third-party OTP accounts.
apps.weak: Push notifications don't arrive or arrive with a delay, authentication loop on phone and laptop, QR scanner freezes after an update, forced notification permission prompt.
apps.whoFor: Strictly Zoho users with no alternative everyone else should use Google Authenticator or Authy.

apps.title: Password Manager & Generator
apps.verdict: A password generator without a real vault it paywalls viewing saved passwords. Review content is nearly empty and users are left confused by the app.
apps.loved: Simple interface is accessible to beginners, a few categories for storing data.
apps.weak: Can't copy a password without a paid subscription. No Sign in with Apple. Interface is not intuitive. Users can't figure out how to use the app.
apps.whoFor: Not a good fit for almost anyone in its current state.

apps.title: Microsoft Authenticator
apps.verdict: Microsoft's corporate authenticator that systematically locks users out when they switch phones. The cycle of 'need a code to log in, need to log in to get a code' is documented in dozens of reviews.
apps.loved: Works steadily as long as you don't need to transfer your account to a new device, protects corporate Microsoft accounts.
apps.weak: The authentication loop on phone changes makes access impossible, codes and notifications periodically fail to arrive, the approval interface is confusing (easy to mix up Deny and Approve), support is unreachable or offers paid assistance.
apps.whoFor: Corporate users whose IT department has issued Microsoft 365 and who have no choice.

quotes.text: Every time I get a new phone, getting my accounts set back up is a nightmare. It wont let you delete and re-add an account. It tries to have you sign in but then it asks for an Authenticator code to complete the sign in process.

scenarios.name: People switching password managers
scenarios.job: Escape a manager that raised its price for the third time in five years without losing hundreds of passwords in the migration
scenarios.gap: In the reviews the barrier to switching comes from a long history and a move done by hand. It is worth checking the completeness of the import, the attachments and the access to the result before giving up the old vault.

scenarios.name: The family administrator
scenarios.job: Keep the whole family’s passwords in one place so the spouse, kids and elderly parents can sign in where they need to without calls asking for help
scenarios.gap: Different family members may need access to different entries. Visibility and the way access is handed over, including in an unforeseen situation, have to be agreed in advance.

scenarios.name: People who need control over where things are stored
scenarios.job: Keep passwords only on their own hardware, no third-party servers, ideally in an open format that can be audited or moved at any moment
scenarios.gap: What matters is the storage place chosen, a format you can follow and the ability to move the data. An open format is useful for control, but on its own it does not prove the whole implementation is secure.

scenarios.name: People restoring access after an incident
scenarios.job: After an account got hacked or a breach notification arrived, finally get organized: different strong passwords everywhere plus two-factor, right now
scenarios.gap: After an incident a person needs to work out the order of actions and restore access to the accounts that matter. A security check based only on a list of passwords should not be promised, or offered in place of help with a compromise.
